result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Credentials & Secrets scope: SecurityConfig.java:29-39 uses BCrypt and a required admin secret placeholder with no embedded secret default. application.properties:14 and application-docker.properties:5 require environment-supplied datasource secrets; docker-compose.yml:7-9,34-36 uses required environment interpolation. .env.example contains explicitly labeled placeholders, not confirmed operational credentials. azure-setup.ps1:15-22,39-41 generates secrets with a cryptographic RNG or accepts environment overrides. No hard-coded authentication secret or cryptographic key was confirmed. Generated .env ACL/mode and deployment umask are not known from static source; omitted restrictive permissions alone are not claimed as a confirmed CWE-732 finding. All values and defaults remain redacted.

Whole-application static analysis of current src/main Java, JavaScript, templates and properties; pom.xml, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, Oracle initialization and Azure PowerShell scripts.

NOT_FOUND means no confirmed matching pattern in the inspected current production/configuration scope, not proof of absence. Tests, generated code, dependencies' implementations, runtime state, history and .github/agents were excluded.

No application code edits, tests, builds, linters, exploit execution or commits. No runtime exploitability verification or dependency CVE audit. Secret values and defaults are omitted from all evidence.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: SecurityConfig.securityFilterChain requires authentication for upload/delete at lines 54-60, making these attributable security-sensitive mutations. PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto records successful uploads with only filename and photo ID at lines 179-180; deletePhoto records only photo ID at line 212, and DetailController.deletePhoto logs only the ID at line 69. These recorded mutation events omit the authenticated principal and originating client, and none of these classes provides audit-context enrichment or an authentication-event listener. Consequently the application-level mutation log cannot attribute changes to a requester or correlate attempts reliably. Framework, reverse-proxy or deployment-specific audit sinks may add coverage, but none is configured in the inspected production files and runtime logging was not observed.

values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
